Incorporating the January 2018 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) into the assessment:

- Business credit: Many banks eased standards/terms for C&I loans—especially to large/middle‑market firms—with narrower loan rate spreads and competition cited as the key driver; some standards were unchanged. Outlooks pointed to possible further easing for small-firm lending and narrower spreads.
- Consumer credit: For credit cards, standards were largely unchanged but several banks tightened specific terms; demand was mixed (unchanged to weaker), and banks expected performance/quality to deteriorate and to tighten standards going forward. HELOC demand was weaker with expected quality deterioration.
- CRE: Banks tightened standards for nonfarm nonresidential and construction/land development loans, reported weaker demand in construction/land development, and expected further tightening.
- Mortgages: Banks expected to ease standards for nonconforming jumbo mortgages.

Integration with the FOMC statement and Financial Stability Report: The SLOOS shows a supportive near-term credit supply for businesses that reinforces the Committee’s “moderate” growth view, while the tightening/quality concerns in unsecured consumer credit and CRE echo the FSR’s highlighted vulnerabilities. Net effect: macro tone remains constructive with gradual hikes appropriate, but with clearer pockets of risk. Slight positive tilt versus the FSR-only read.
